 YTL Corp posts stronger quarterly performance across operations

 | 5:38 PM MYT

 YTL Corporation Bhd executive chairman Tan Sri Francis Yeoh Sock Ping. 
 PETALING JAYA: YTL Corp Bhd saw a better performance on a whole in its latest quarter due to better performance recorded across all operations.
 For the first quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (1Q26), the conglomerate’s net profit was up by 5% year-on-year (y-o-y) to RM700.1mil. Revenue for the quarter grew by 34% y-o-y to RM10.2bil, due to better performance recorded across all business segments.
 Executive chairman, Tan Sri (Sir) Francis Yeoh Sock Ping said the group made a strong start to its 2027 financial year.
 “The increase in segment profit was contributed mainly by the construction, cement and management services segments,” he said in a statement.
 YTL Power International Bhd posted a 7% y-o-y drop in net profit to RM451.7mil. This was despite a 41 y-o-y increase in revenue to RM7.5bil. Yeoh said the earnings in the power generation and water and sewerage segments moderated. This, he added, is partially countered by the increased contribution from the data center segment with the progressive completion and occupancy ramp-up of additional data halls.
 As for the group’s cement division, Malayan Cement Bhd ’s net profit expanded by 13% y-o-y to RM227.8mil. Revenue increased by 9% y-o-y to RM1.3bil.
 Yeoh said this division’s performance was partially offset by the higher transportation and energy costs.
 “Notwithstanding the increase in operating costs, the Group remained committed to rigorous cost management and operational efficiency initiatives, including the increased adoption of renewable energy and waste heat recovery and utilisation of alternative fuels and raw materials.
 “These ongoing efforts, coupled with its lower carbon product portfolio, comprising ECOCem, ECOConcrete, ECODrymix and ECOSand, help the group in maintaining its cost competitiveness amid a challenging cost environment,” he said.
 Meanwhile, YTL Hospitality REIT ’s net property income (NPI) contracted by 4% y-o-y to RM74mil in 1Q26. Revenue decreased by 0.43% y-o-y to RM139.9mil in 3Q26.
 Yeoh said the hotel segment’s lower performance was primarily due to reduced international visitor activity in the absence of major events. Meanwhile, the property rental segment registered higher revenue and NPI resulting mainly from new rental income following commencement of the AC Hotel Puchong lease agreement in April 2026.
